top.line: The php2shell story at 8pm, a guided tour of the site built in a day, and what changed by 22:00.
top.para: At 8pm UK time the fix is out, sixteen agencies say install it, attackers are trying, and no named organisation has said php2shell was the way in. The Dutch inventory lists 724 products, 61 fixed. The tour covers php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai, built in 34 versions in a day; updates add the compromise map, v0.6.0 and a correction on the source watch.

in-short.line: Seven lines: the fix, attempts, no named compromise, the inventory, a site in a day, a public vault, versions.
in-short.para: Install PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Attempts number in the millions, one seen four days early. No named organisation says it was compromised through these flaws, which are not on the US exploited list. 724 products listed, 61 fixed. The site was built today in 34 versions, on a public vault, with versions recorded.

stands.line: Fix since 21 October, unanimous advice to install, mass attempts, no named compromise, 724 inventory rows.
stands.para: Two flaws rated 9.2, fixed on 21 October; 8.1 and older have no fix. Disclosure was 21 October, not 22, which our section had wrong. Agencies agree on patching, not on going offline. Cloudflare reports millions of attempts, Amazon one on 17 October. No named organisation had said it was compromised, and the US catalogue does not list the flaws.

unknown.line: Unknown: break-ins, unpatched counts, the leak and the 70% figure; the incomplete-fix report was answered.
unknown.para: Nobody yet knows whether any site was broken into before patching. The report that the fix was incomplete was answered by PHP's security team at 09:11 UTC as an unrelated crash bug, which the 8pm version missed. The number of unpatched systems is an open contradiction, the 20 October leak's source is unknown, and 70% is a share of websites, not risk.

day.line: From v0.1.0 at 09:27 to v0.5.5 at 19:04 UTC: 34 versions, 62 commits, 17 team members.
day.para: The site went from its first to its thirty-fourth version in one day, with two version lines merged. Its team page lists two people and 13 agents, each with a role, rules and shipped work, and a board of 89 tasks, 25 done. The editor directed by memo; the agents captured, built, checked and released.

tour.line: Eleven stops: readers, phone, evidence, graded claims, graph, code, patching, stories, versions, vaults, readers.
tour.para: A plain-English front page and fifteen briefings; Now and Ask on a phone with your own key; a public vault of 184 sources and a source watch of 773 pages; 70 claims graded, two refuted, ten contradictions; a 209-node graph; the fix read in php-src; the inventory hour by hour; stories; 110 versioned sections; eight vaults; synthetic readers.

map.line: A snapshot of every version, head, count and file hash at 8pm, so the next update is a diff.
map.para: Published with this article: the site's version and commit, the vault, source watch and inventory heads and counts, the fact-check run, the outside checks, every count in the tour and the hash of all 46 data files. The next update takes the same snapshot, and the difference is the update.

lessons.line: The pages lag the evidence, grading caught our own error, and versions make updates exact.
lessons.para: The 8pm claim that capture stopped was wrong: the evidence vault's last capture is 11:34 UTC, but the source watch ran into the evening, reaching 773 pages and 1,851 snapshots, and the vendor reports were captured by 11:30. The site's copies lag behind. The fact-check desk refuted a date in our section, now corrected. Versioning makes changes exact.

limits.line: Facts are as captured; two checks are mine at 19:00; counts at v0.5.5; grades are one run.
limits.para: The evidence vault's latest capture is 11:34 UTC, and the source watch's runs continued into the evening. The exploited-vulnerability catalogue and php.net were read directly at 19:00 and are not captured. Counts are from the site's data at 19:04 UTC. The grades are one desk's single run, and synthetic readers are a test instrument, not readers.

sources.line: The site and its repository, the public vault, the Dutch inventory, CISA and php.net, and screenshots.
sources.para: Sources: php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai at v0.5.5 and its repository, the evidence vault cloned with its public read key at 31ccc515c29f, the NCSC-NL inventory at 94b4b16, CISA's catalogue feed and php.net's news read at 19:00 UTC, and screenshots taken at 19:06 UTC, with earlier articles on the story.

since.line: By 22:00 the site reached v0.6.0: a compromise map, a second fact-check run, risk registers and more readers.
since.para: The compromise map, as of 20:50 UTC, searched widely and found millions of attempts, three vendors reporting unnamed exploitation, one stopped attack, and no organisation naming php2shell as the way in. Fact-check run 2 found the incomplete-fix answer; KEV still lists neither flaw at 22:09. A GRC section maps 34 risks to 95 controls. Telemetry reached 161 sessions.
